title: Enhancing Linux Privilege Escalation Attack Capabilities of Local LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2604.27143v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Cloud-based Large Language Models (LLMs) can perform autonomous penetration-testing sub-tasks such as Linux privilege escalation, but raise security, privacy, and sovereignty concerns. Locally hosted open-weight models avoid these issues, yet prior work reports that small open-weight models succeed on only 8-16% of standardized privilege-escalation tasks, far below frontier cloud models. This paper is an empirical study of why small models fail at this task and which engineering techniques close the gap. From execution traces we distill six recurring failure modes, map each to an established enhancement technique, and evaluate five (chain-of-thought prompting, retrieval-augmented generation, structured prompting, history compression, and reflective analysis) as reproducible extensions to the open-source hackingBuddyGPT framework. translated_title: 增强本地LLM代理的Linux权限提升攻击能力
translated_abstract: 摘要：基于云的大语言模型（LLMs）能够执行自主渗透测试子任务，如Linux权限提升，但引发了安全、隐私和主权方面的担忧。本地托管的开源权重模型避免了这些问题，然而先前的研究报告指出，小型开源权重模型在标准化权限提升任务上的成功率仅为8-16%，远低于前沿云模型。本文是一项实证研究，探讨小型模型在此任务中失败的原因，以及哪些工程技术能缩小这一差距。通过执行轨迹，我们提炼出六种常见的失败模式，将每种模式映射到一种成熟的增强技术，并评估了五种技术（链式思维提示、检索增强生成、结构化提示、历史压缩和反思性分析）作为开源hackingBuddyGPT框架的可复现扩展。在单一共享测试平台和匹配条件下，我们评估的技术集合将两个...
tldr: 本文通过实证研究识别小型本地LLM在Linux权限提升任务中的六种失败模式，并验证五种增强技术，显著提升其攻击能力，缩小与云模型的差距。
en_tdlr: This paper empirically identifies six failure modes of small local LLMs in Linux privilege escalation tasks and validates five enhancement techniques, significantly improving their attack capability and narrowing the gap with cloud models.
